call_chain_analysis: bestzip's main module (lib/bestzip.js) exports a top-level `zip` function and three secondary functions: `nativeZip`, `nodeZip`, `hasNativeZip`. The top-level `zip` branches on `hasNativeZip()` (which does `which.sync("zip", { nothrow: true })`). On the Jazzer.js sandbox image there is no `zip` binary on PATH, so `hasNativeZip()` returns false and `zip()` dispatches to `nodeZip`, which uses the `archiver` package and never calls `child_process.exec` — the sink at line 27 is unreachable through that path. The fix is to call `module.exports.nativeZip` directly. Inside `nativeZip` (lib/bestzip.js:19-41), the code builds `const command = `zip --quiet --recurse-paths ${options.destination} ${sources}`` (lines 23-26), where `sources` is `Array.isArray(options.source) ? options.source.join(" ") : options.source`, and then calls `const zipProcess = cp.exec(command, { stdio: "inherit", cwd: options.cwd });` at line 27:27 — the sink. Both `options.destination` and `options.source` are spliced into the shell command string with no quoting or escaping. Jazzer.js's CommandInjection bug detector hooks `child_process.exec` and inspects the command string synchronously on the call, before the OS process is spawned, so detection fires regardless of whether the `zip` binary exists; the subsequent async rejection from the missing binary is irrelevant to the detector.
argument_reasoning: The fuzzer-controlled bytes have to appear as an unescaped substring in the final command string so Jazzer.js's CommandInjection detector can match its sentinel (`jaz_zer`). We pass the fuzzer input via `options.source` as a plain string, so it is interpolated raw after `--recurse-paths out.zip ` in the command. We use `provider.consumeRemainingAsString()` to hand the fuzzer maximum entropy for the whole substring. Node's `child_process.exec` rejects any command string containing a NUL byte with `TypeError: argument 'command' must be a string without null bytes` — that TypeError throws synchronously inside `nativeZip`, bubbles into our try/catch, and never reaches the detector, so we strip NULs with `.replace(/\u0000/g, "")`. `destination` and `cwd` are set to constant benign values (`"out.zip"`, `"/tmp"`); they still appear in the command string but do not need to carry fuzz input. We swallow the promise rejection from the (absent) `zip` binary with `p.catch(() => {})` so the fuzzer keeps evolving inputs; by then the exec hook has already seen the command string.

lessons: The 7B v4 model generated structurally valid code but did not reach the sink (P1 reach gap). The most likely reason is that the model called the top-level `require('bestzip')(options)` export, which is gated by `hasNativeZip()` / `which.sync("zip")`. The Jazzer.js sandbox has no `zip` binary installed, so the gate flips to `nodeZip`, a pure-Node pipeline that uses `fs.createWriteStream` + archiver and never calls `child_process.exec` — the sink at lib/bestzip.js:27 is unreachable via that branch. Lesson: when a package has a feature-detection gate guarding the sink and the sandbox would fail the gate, inspect the module exports for a direct handle to the gated code path. Here `module.exports.nativeZip = nativeZip;` makes the native branch callable with no gate, and Jazzer's `exec` hook fires synchronously on the call so the (absent) OS binary never matters. Secondary lesson: Node's `exec` rejects NUL bytes synchronously with a TypeError that pre-empts the detector, so strip them from fuzzer input for any shell-string sink.
